diagrams.title: Geräte-Reservierung und Request-Ledger
diagrams.lead: Eine Reservierung ist ein ablaufendes, kooperatives Recht auf Eingaben an ein Gerät. Das Ledger merkt sich jeden mutierenden Aufruf mit request_id vor dem Senden, damit eine Wiederholung nach verlorener Antwort beantwortet statt erneut gesendet wird.

nodes.title: Übernahme: für die Person gedacht, nicht erzwungen
Kooperativ: schützt zwischen Tomacco-Clients, nicht gegen adb, SSH, fastboot oder Agenten ohne Tomacco
Eingabe mit ungültigem Token: reservation_expired · _released · _revoked · _not_held. Lesen bleibt erlaubt
pending: vor dem Senden auf Platte
pending: nicht erneut senden, später fragen
Beobachten; nie blind wiederholen, nie anderer Transport
Keine genau-einmal-Garantie; Ledger 24 h ohne Tipptext und Token. Hat der Worker eine Eingabe verbucht, wird unknown zu completed abgeglichen

notes: Das Token sieht nur, wer acquire oder takeover aufruft; gespeichert wird sein SHA-256, nie das Token selbst. takeover ist eine normale destruktive Operation: Agenten sollen die Person fragen, statt sie zu nutzen.

Eine Ablehnung, die nachweislich nichts gesendet hat (Reservierung, frame_stale, policy_denied …), wird als refused gespeichert und ist lesbar. Dieselbe request_id mit gleicher Absicht übernimmt den Eintrag und führt erneut aus.

demo.capabilities meldet Ton-Modi und source_available. Fehlt der lokale AAC-Encoder, bleiben stumme MP4s und PNG-Vorschauen möglich; nur source-MP4 wird vor dem Job abgelehnt. Vorschau-PNGs bleiben stumme Einzelbilder, auch wenn die Szene source speichert.

Video-Zeit: ffmpeg sucht mit clip.start, rebasiert den ersten dekodierten Videoframe und rastert auf Ausgabe-fps. Der Schnitt kann an die Quell-Zeitbasis und Framedauer gebunden sein; Posen werden auf den exakten Ausgabezeitpunkten i/fps interpoliert. Höhere Ausgabe-fps schaffen keine neuen Bewegungsdetails.

Originalton wird auf denselben tatsächlich beobachteten Video-Ursprung gelegt: copyts/start_at_zero und der erste Frame-PTS desselben Decoderlaufs, nicht pauschal clip.start oder der erste Audio-PTS. Der begrenzte showinfo-Seitenzweig protokolliert nur diesen Frame. Das Manifest hält source_audio_origin fest.

Nur die erste Quell-Audiospur wird als AAC, 48 kHz und Stereo ausgegeben. Führende Lücken, kurze Audiospuren oder ein Ausschnitt nach deren Ende werden mit Stille bis zur gerasterten Videodauer gefüllt. Das Video wird weder verkürzt noch durch -shortest beendet. Externe Musik, Pegelregler und Audio-Mixing sind nicht enthalten.

Unabhängige Abnahme prüft Stream-Anzahl, H.264/yuv420p, AAC-Format, Start/Dauer und den vollständigen Decode beider Streams. silent, audio.mode, Szenen-Revision und Renderer-Manifest müssen zusammenpassen. Ausgabe, Poster und Manifest werden erst nach erfolgreicher Prüfung veröffentlicht; demo.export.inspect prüft Medien und Belege erneut.

Bestehende Grenzen: eine lokale Aufnahme je Szene; Modelle phone/tablet, QPainter-Perspektive ohne importierte Modelle oder GPU-Szene. 320–3840 px (gerade), 24/25/30/60 fps, 0,1–60 s, maximal 120 Posen. Quelle bleibt unverändert. Live-Aufnahme, Mehrfach-Clips, Übergänge, Audio-Mixing und frei steuerbare 3D-Szenen bleiben Folgeschritte.

Ausgabe, Poster und Manifest müssen neue Pfade sein, auch nach Ja im Ersetzen-Dialog (D19). dieselbe request_id gibt den bekannten Job zurück; eine andere Absicht unter derselben ID oder ein belegtes Ziel wird mit demo_conflict abgelehnt. operations.title: Build & run on device
operations.description: Build and deploy to a selected Android/iOS device. With device virtual-iphone, an xtool project is built with xtool dev build and installed and opened on the running virtual iPhone with ios.virtual.deploy, which skips the install when the signed app is unchanged; then, after crash_check_seconds, its crash reports are read, and a report that was not there before the deploy fails the job as crashed. The job writes build/tomacco/virtual_iphone_run.json in the project: state (launched, crashed, failed, or building when the build failed), build_seconds, deploy (job_id, seconds, unchanged, steps), pid and crash_check. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off. Flutter supports interactive hot reload via job.send. While a Flutter session runs, job.get's result.flutter has the app's VM service URI (vm_service_uri, and vm_service_http_uri for a browser) and, once Flutter reports them, devtools_uri, devtools_app_uri (DevTools opened on this app) and dtd_uri. operations.description: Watch a project's source files and, whenever they change and have stayed unchanged for debounce_ms, build, install and launch the app again with project.run, as a durable job; it also runs the app once at the start. Build output, dependency and tool directories (build, .gradle, .dart_tool, node_modules, Pods, .git and others) are ignored. For a Flutter project it starts one Flutter session and sends it Hot Reload on each change, starting a new session when that one has ended. operations.title: Run steps in order
operations.description: Run a short list of operations in order in one call and return each step's result. A step that starts a job is followed until the job ends, or until its app is up (phase ready), unless the step sets wait false; the first step that fails, or whose job does not succeed, stops the rest and answers workflow_step_failed with every step so far under details.steps and the steps not run under details.skipped. A destructive step, and one that publishes (play.commit, an upload with ios.store_ship or apple.store), runs only with its own confirm true; without it nothing runs and the answer is workflow_needs_confirmation. An argument value {"from_step": N, "pointer": "/result/..."} is replaced by that JSON pointer into step N's record, such as /result/artifacts/0/path of a finished build. Unknown operations and wrong arguments are refused before the first step. When timeout runs out the current job keeps running.

operations.title: Run native tests
operations.description: Run JSON native UI scenarios (one file, or a directory of them) across devices with device locks, JUnit, JSON reports, failure screenshots and a self-contained report.html; each run's outcomes are added to the test history (testing.history). A device is an Android serial or virtual-iphone, the running virtual iPhone. By default every device runs every scenario; shard splits the scenarios across the devices and merges their results into one report. With retries, a failed scenario runs again; each result lists its attempts and flaky marks a pass after a failure. Besides selector steps, a scenario can tap and swipe at pixel coordinates, type text, send a key, pause, take a screenshot, assert_screen (compare the screen with a baseline PNG), wait_screen (until it matches), wait_text (until text is on the screen, or with state absent gone; from the UI hierarchy on Android, read with Tesseract where there is none or source is ocr) and wait_stable (until the screen has not changed for duration milliseconds). On Android, a measure step records startup, frames, memory or usage metrics of an app, and a budget fails the scenario as budget_exceeded when a metric is outside it. On the virtual iPhone, steps go through ios.emulator.control at pixels of ios.virtual.screenshot, launch opens an app through the guest, and stop, clear and measure fail, and so do selector steps other than a text or text_contains selector, which is read off the screenshot with Tesseract (pixel-based; wait and assert, click and long_click, not fill): the guest reports no UI hierarchy. Its crash reports are not read after a scenario; use testing.crashes. With platform ios, it runs the same scenarios on USB iPhones through the WebDriverAgent session runtime.start keeps for each device (start it first): selectors are read against WDA's XML source, visible elements only, with text as the label (or the value of an element without one), resource_id as the accessibility identifier, description as the label and class as the element type; tap and swipe coordinates are in points; keys are home, enter, backspace, delete or tab. clickable, checked and package selectors and the clear step are refused there, and crashes are not read.

operations.title: Record UI test
operations.description: Record a UI test on an Android device or the virtual iPhone. Between start and stop, the taps, swipes, text and keys sent to the device through android.input, runtime.input (the desktop's live display included) and testing.action become testing.run scenario steps. A tap becomes a click on the element under it, named by resource ID, description or text (with index when that is shared), when the UI hierarchy read just before the tap names one; otherwise a tap at pixel coordinates. Reading the hierarchy makes each tap slower while recording. stop writes the scenario to path; status counts the steps; discard throws the recording away. Input a scenario cannot express, such as a rotation, is listed under skipped. With device virtual-iphone (while it runs), start notes the screen's size and the ios.emulator.control input sent to its guest job becomes steps at pixel coordinates: click a tap, drag a swipe, a streamed touch_down to touch_up a tap, long press or swipe, and text, key and home their steps; a key combination and power_button are skipped.

operations.description: Read logcat's crash, system and main buffers and return Java crashes (FATAL EXCEPTION), ANRs and native crashes (Fatal signal) as structured events with package, pid, exception, message, stack and reason. operations.title: Measure app startup
operations.description: Launch an app several times and report each launch's time in milliseconds with count, min, max, mean, median and p90. On Android it reads am start -W's TotalTime and WaitTime: cold stops the app before each launch; warm keeps the process and recreates the activity; hot returns to the running activity from the home screen. Each run lists the launch state Android reported, and mismatched_runs counts launches whose state differs from mode. On an iPhone (platform ios with its UDID, through go-ios) or the virtual iPhone (device virtual-iphone) there is no launch timer, so the screen is timed: from the open request to the first picture that differs from the one before and stays different (first_frame_ms, the startup_<mode>_* metrics), to the request returning with the app's process (launched_ms) and to the screen keeping still for settle_ms (settled_ms); modes are cold (the app's process ended first: go-ios kill, or restart_ui on the virtual iPhone) and hot (sent to the background and opened again), and launch_state compares the app's process with the one before. iPhone times are coarse (resolution_ms); virtual-iPhone times are emulated and far slower than an iPhone's. metrics (startup_<mode>_median_ms and others) feed profile.compare and profile.budget; report saves the result as JSON.

operations.title: Ordered input batch
operations.description: Run up to 50 input and wait steps in order on one session, in one call, with a result per step. A text step waits until a field has the focus (polling the session's focus and keyboard) before it types, so the first characters are not lost, and answers focus_timeout with nothing typed when no field takes it; where the transport cannot report focus it says so and settles briefly instead. A tap can name a mark from the last screen.marks of this session and is verified like screen.tap. A step may carry expect, a text that must appear or go afterwards: met makes the step verified, otherwise postcondition_failed stops the batch with the step still counted as applied. A fill step with verify_value is verified only when the field's exact value was read back; text sent with an unknown effect makes it uncertain (field_uncertain) and it is never sent again. The first failure stops the rest: the error's details list every step so far (steps), the indexes that reached the device (applied_steps), those whose effect is unknown (uncertain_steps) and those not run (skipped), so an agent never resends an applied step. The whole batch is bounded by timeout and by the client's cancellation. With frame (width, height, orientation from runtime.observe) the batch is refused with frame_stale and nothing sent when the screen's geometry changed since. observe_after appends a fresh runtime.observe. The answer's evidence is fixture on the offline fixture runtime. With reservation_token it acts under a device reservation (device.reservation.acquire); with request_id it is recorded once in the request ledger, so a repeat after a lost answer is not sent again.

operations.title: Operate running virtual iOS
operations.description: Inspect, capture or send input to a live ios.emulator.paravirtual job started with interactive=true. Actions are serialized per guest: one that arrives while another runs waits up to 2.5 s for its turn before ios_control_busy is returned. ios_control_starting means the control monitor is not published yet; ios_control_ended means the emulator has exited while the job is still finishing (hashing its media), so wait for the job instead of cancelling it. Coordinates are normalized from 0 to 1 across the captured display. With input_transport=virtio, click/drag use an absolute mouse. With usb-hid, they use a single touchscreen contact; home sends the HID Consumer Menu usage with emulator-owned release, and status reports actual USB delivery counters. Touch has no hover or multitouch. A persistent client (tomaccoctl mcp) can stream a live contact instead: touch_down presses at x/y and holds the guest's control lane until touch_up, touch_move moves the contact (the same point again only keeps it alive), and touch_up lifts it, at x/y when given. Other control actions wait for that lane meanwhile; file frames do not. A contact without any event for 5 s is lifted, and the client's end lifts whatever it still holds. A one-shot call refuses touch_down with ios_touch_lane_required; touch_up is accepted anywhere and always sends a release. A drag lifts at its end point at once, which a scroll view reads as a fling; with hold_ms it first rests there that long, so the content stops where the contact did. power_button sends the native timed 100 ms GPIO side-button pulse only on the tomacco-vphone machine; it can wake or lock the screen, so acknowledgement never establishes the resulting screen state. key accepts QEMU key names. Input acknowledgement is not proof of a guest UI response; inspect a subsequent screenshot. Screenshots stay in the owned job directory. frame returns an actual PNG data_url (up to 16 MiB) and deletes its temporary capture on success or failure; it is suitable for bounded live preview polling. metrics reads actual QMP CPU state/topology, cumulative block-device I/O counters and TCG cache statistics without pausing or resetting the guest. Host sampling timestamps bound the sequential observations. Unknown TCG fields stay null, unavailable monitor statistics retain their error, and the original text is preserved. Counters and guest-clock lag are not application FPS or CPU utilization. stop requests QMP exit so the durable job can finalize media hashes. With guest control enabled it reserves the framework lane and requires a confirmed idle native worker; pending or unknown work prevents stopping. An acknowledgement does not establish guest OS shutdown or completed storage verification. Follow ios.emulator.report until the job ends; an unconfirmed stop is not replayed automatically. If the emulator cannot be told to exit, the stop record is rewritten without the flush confirmation (guest_storage_flushed false, quit_acknowledged false); a request the client cancels leaves no record and does not stop the emulator. trust_cache_update stops the guest's CPUs, replaces the boot's trust-cache module in guest RAM with the file at path and lets them go on; only for a machine built with vphone-trust-cache-update, and ios.virtual.deploy is the way to use it. text types on the USB keyboard, into what has the focus; a key sent before the field has it is lost, so look at a frame first. iOS reads the keys with the layout of the guest's language: layout follows it unless named. Input actions (click, drag, text, key, home, power_button, move, touch_*) take reservation_token and request_id.

operations.title: Control native iOS guest programs
operations.description:
Call the owned guest service through the active job's private virtio-vsock channel. Requires build_guest_tools agent=true and paravirtual guest_control_backend. One framework request and one status, service-log or cancel request may run at once; nothing connects from outside. Framework requests return request_id: ios.emulator.guest_result follows the latest receipt after a timeout without replaying the request. A timed-out mutation may still execute in iOS and is never replayed automatically. status reports the current worker and, as *_supported flags, what these guest tools offer. Acceptance never verifies a visible scene, and a process or crash observation never proves a process lifetime.
Apps: inspect lists LaunchServices inventory; lookup finds a bundle; install takes a guest .app or .ipa through MobileInstallation (an IPA needs bundle_id) with request-correlated progress; register and open start an app through the original FrontBoard service, keeping native errors and the app's PID; cancel stops the current worker. receive_bundle, policy_add and debug_server are the guest side of ios.virtual.deploy and ios.virtual.debug.
Logs: logs reads bounded owned logs by name, among them development (signing setup and verifier), quiet (tomacco-quiet: services unloaded and its locationd guard), battery, debugserver and buffer_texture (the native Metal buffer-texture observer), and an application's log through its container.
Setup: setup reads SetupAssistant and MobileActivation state. setup_finish, on an activated virtual device, backs up and writes the three setup values through cfprefsd and reads them back; it returns restart_required. restart_ui restarts the interface. flush flushes storage. effects reduced or original sets Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion through the system's setters, which turns the glass materials the renderer cannot draw correctly into plain surfaces. watchdog_scale original or a factor 2..30 sets FrontBoard's FBLaunchWatchdogScale, applied after restart_ui or a reboot; the watchdogs stay active. icon_cache clear moves each IconsCache store aside, deleting nothing, and restarts SpringBoard so that every icon is rendered again. time_zone Area/City sets the system zone through tzlink and reads previous_link and link back. auto_lock never or original sets Settings' Auto-Lock through ManagedConfiguration, or SBDontLockEver when profiled does not take it, and reads it back. Setting a zone or Auto-Lock again is harmless, so a lost reply is automatic_retry_safe; a start sends both itself.
State: screen_state reads SpringBoard's screen-lock, passcode and backlight state; a failed RPC stays unknown, never unlocked. display_state reads the MobileGestalt scale and display tuple against the chosen display-scale. display_refresh asks the system helper to rebuild its display cache after checking the scale locally, and a new display_state must confirm it before a UI restart. foreground_state reads SpringBoard's primary-layout application. graphics_state reads the Metal default device and a process-name snapshot without submitting GPU work. surface_state reads IOSurface metadata for up to four comma-separated decimal IDs; no pixels are accessed. network_state lists the interfaces' IPv4 addresses and tries one name lookup. hardware_probe <IOKit class> counts that class's services. gestalt <key> reads one MobileGestalt answer. developer_mode status or enable reads or arms Developer Mode, effective at the next boot. keyboard_layout reports the guest's language, by whose layout iOS reads a hardware keyboard.
Diagnostics: crash_reports <report name prefix> reads the matching .ips and .crash files of the CrashReporter directories, up to 512 KiB as base64 and with crash_report_identities parsed from the reports; it never removes reports. persistence_probe takes create:<64 hex digits>, read:<same challenge>, classes:<challenge> (one file per protection class A..D) or inode:<digits> (a path and protection class for a boot log's failure). A clean-reboot result needs two separately bound boots with the same challenge.

operations.title: Virtual iOS device: status
operations.description: Read whether a virtual iOS device profile is configured, its current run, phase, guest job and any start or stop that is in progress. A guest job started from another data directory has no guest_state here; that is unknown, not stopped. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. Also reports model (for the next start), running_model (of the current run), running_panel (the current run's panel as WIDTHxHEIGHT@HZ:WIDTH_MMxHEIGHT_MM, as its guest job's request gave it to the engine, so a later edit of the profile does not change it; null when that boot named no panel. Without a guest job: the model's own panel, or the profile's display profile for the Home-button phone; null for an unknown recorded model), models (the choice: id, name, panel, and source apple or derived) and guest_ended when the guest has ended on its own since the last start, with guest_saved telling whether it flushed its storage and closed cleanly first (as a session does at its time limit). application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. applications lists the developer apps the profile names (bundle path, bundle_id); the start installs them from the guest-tools build that carries them. phase_started and phase_elapsed_seconds tell when the current phase began and how long it has run, and phases lists each phase of the current start or stop with its started time and seconds (empty for a state written before phases were logged). start_timing and stop_timing break the last start and stop down into steps with their seconds (start: checks, preparation, disk_copy with its method, guest_tools, boot_request, input_hashing with its bytes, launcher, boot, app_install, guest_settings, unlock_and_launch, display_check; stop: guest_exit, output_hashing, finalize), with total_seconds, slowest and run; a step whose times are unknown is folded into the next one, which lists it under includes; null before the first start that recorded them. copy_progress, only in the preparing phase, compares the bytes of the new disk copy with those of its base (bytes_done, bytes_total, percent) and names the preparation's step and disk; a reflinked copy is complete at once. start_disk says whether the next start's disk copy fits in the profile's installs: needed_bytes, free_bytes, reclaimable_bytes (older copies the start deletes first), reflink and enough, the check ios.virtual.start refuses with; the status writes nothing to find out, so on a filesystem that might clone files and lacks room for a full copy enough and reflink are null until a start probes it. start_disk.method is how that start makes its root disk (copy, overlay or flatten), and start_disks the profile's choice (copy or overlay). Null when the base's disks or the filesystem cannot be read. last_run says in plain words how the last finished run ended: verified, the launcher's outcome, a summary, each reason it was not verified (no exit code 0, incomplete storage hashes, no confirmed flush, the graphics memory guard) and a remedy; null before the first run that recorded it. next names what to call when a start or stop ended halfway, with action (resume, unlock_then_resume, stop, record_end, start_again or wait), call, arguments, resumes (true when the call goes on with the running guest without a new disk copy) and why; null when nothing is left halfway. host reports on every call the graphics card's memory (gpu: source guard, the running guest's last guard check, or sysfs, the card with the most memory; used_bytes, total_bytes, free_bytes, guard_limit_free_bytes, the eighth the graphics memory guard keeps, level ok, low under a quarter free or short under the guard's limit, and short_checks and guard_stopping from the guard; null when no card reports memory) and the host's pressure (pressure: Linux PSI full avg10 and avg60 for io and memory against the start's admission limits, blocked naming those over them, observed false without PSI). liveness, while the guest runs, says whether it still shows signs of life: state live, quiet (no new frame, console output or guest answer for stall_seconds; normal for a still screen), stalled (the guest service did not answer a probe and neither it nor the screen showed life for stall_seconds) or booting (not judged); last_seen with the newest frame's number, the console log's size and the guest's last answer, each with when it last changed; and for a stalled phone recovery, the typed calls to make in order: ios.emulator.guest restart_ui, then ios.virtual.stop. The status never acts on the phone itself; it remembers the signs in liveness.json in the guest job's run directory.

operations.title: Check this machine for the virtual iOS device
operations.description: Check whether this machine can run the virtual iOS device, before any setup step or start: architecture (x86_64), CPU (logical processors, VT-x or AMD-V, AVX2), /dev/kvm for the disk-preparing helper, memory (fail under 12 GiB, warn under 16 GiB), free disk on the filesystem of directory (by default the configured profile's installs, needing 32 GiB for one start's disk copy, else the data directory, needing 100 GiB for the setup chain), Vulkan drivers and the card with the most graphics memory (fail under 8 GiB, warn under 16 GiB or when under an eighth is free), the helper support's APFS module against the running kernel, and passt for the guest network. Each entry in checks has check, status (pass, warn or fail), found, message and a remedy unless it passed; ready is false when any check fails. host has logical_cpus, physical_cores (one per package and core among the CPUs this process may use) and memory_total_bytes, and recommend compares the configured profile's boot settings with them: each entry names a setting (boot.host_cpu_policy: performance with at least two physical cores more than application processors, scheduler with fewer cores than processors; boot.translation_cache_mib: 1024 under 16 GiB of memory, 2048 from 32 GiB), its current and suggested value and the reason; empty when they suit the host or no profile is configured. Nothing is changed. Reads /proc, /sys, PATH and the filesystem only; starts and writes nothing. A pass means the machine meets what the device was measured with, not that it was qualified on it.

operations.title: Start virtual iOS device
operations.description: Start the configured virtual iOS device as one durable job: prepare a new private disk copy from the last cleanly closed run (reinstalling guest tools and restoring the Preboot Metal driver the guest removes), boot it, attempt passcode-free unlock with Home presses and request the configured app once the native screen-state query confirms unlock. Launch acceptance does not establish a visible application scene. A guest that is already running is adopted. Disks of a run that did not close with verified storage are never reused. Follow progress with ios.virtual.status and job.logs. Experimental research runtime: the boot takes many minutes and the guest runs several times slower than real time. A late screen-query receipt is followed by its original request ID. application_process reports only the matching active job and application; it proves no process lifetime or visible scene. A start that would make a disk copy is refused with ios_virtual_disk_space, before anything is deleted or copied, when the filesystem of the profile's installs lacks the base's disks plus 1 GiB, counting the older copies the start deletes first; a filesystem that clones files (reflink) needs only the 1 GiB. A start that boots a guest returns warnings, a list of {check, message}: check gpu when under a quarter of the graphics card is free (the graphics memory guard stops a session under an eighth), check pressure when the host's I/O or memory pressure is over the admission limits the start waits for; neither refuses the start. Refused with ios_virtual_host_too_small on a host that is not x86_64 or has less than 12 GiB of memory.

operations.title: Clean up virtual iOS device disk copies

Each copy's files are locked before it is deleted, so a copy a running guest holds is refused with the reason. A guest-install* directory the state does not record is listed under unrecorded and never deleted. copies lists each candidate with path, bytes (allocated on disk; blocks a reflinked copy shares with its base are counted in full) and removed; reclaimable_bytes is their sum and freed_bytes what was deleted. operations.title: Install app on running virtual iOS device
operations.description: One step from a built .app directory to the app on the running phone, without a reboot: inspect the bundle, sign a copy ad hoc, exchange spare entries of this boot's trust cache for its hashes while the guest is stopped for a moment, send it over the guest channel, name it to the signing adapter, install it through installd and open it. A durable job: follow job.logs, whose deploy events carry each step's seconds. When this run installed the same signed app before (the cdhash of the ad hoc signed copy, which seals every file of the bundle), nothing is trusted, sent or installed: the deploy event unchanged follows signed and the app is only opened; force installs it again. The profile lists the app afterwards, so the next start stages it. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off: use ios.virtual.configure add_application and start it. A boot has 512 spare entries and the adapter's table of the boot takes 32 apps, frameworks and extensions.

operations.title: Debug process on virtual iOS device
operations.description: Join lldb to one process of the running phone: a durable job holds a TCP port on the host's loopback and, once lldb connects, copies its bytes to /usr/libexec/debugserver in the guest, attached to the target. The first line of job.logs is an event with the port and the lldb command, process connect connect://127.0.0.1:<port>. The app needs get-task-allow (ios.virtual.deploy with such entitlements). One session per job; it ends when lldb disconnects. Anything that reaches this port controls that process, so it listens on loopback only.

operations.title: Save crash reports of virtual iOS device
operations.description: Read the running virtual iPhone's crash reports whose file names start with process (an app's executable name, or any report name prefix) through the guest service, as ios.emulator.guest crash_reports does, and keep each complete one as a file on the host at directory/<owner>/<name> (owner mobile or root). reports lists every match: owner, name, path, bytes, sha256, saved, and the pid, process, capture_time and incident_id parsed from its bytes; a report the guest could not read whole, or with a name or owner that is not a plain report name, has saved false, no path and the reason. operations.title: Log of virtual iOS device
operations.description: Read the configured virtual iPhone's log as structured lines: the guest's serial console (uart.log of its guest job, running or last), where the kernel prints and launchd forwards log records. Each line has offset (its byte offset), time (as the line gives it, or null), process (for a launchd record the service's last label part, for a UIKit application its executable-like last identifier part; kernel for a line of no known form), pid, service, sender (the forwarding subsystem or the library in name(library)[pid]), level (emergency, alert, critical, error, fault, warning, notice, info, debug, default, or null) and message (cut at 2000 characters). bundle_id keeps one app's lines, across relaunches, and the reply names its executable under app; refused with ios_virtual_application_unknown for an app the profile does not list. Without offset the last 256 KiB are read; pass next_offset back to follow the log. Only complete lines are returned; an unfinished one comes in a later read. more says a read stopped at max_lines or 1 MiB before the end; reset says an offset past the end (another run's log) started over at 0. job_id names the guest job read and running whether it still runs. Reads a host file; the guest is not asked. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when no run has a guest job and ios_virtual_log_unavailable before the console log exists.

operations.title: Screenshot of virtual iOS device
operations.description: Save the running virtual iPhone's current screen as a PNG at path, from the same frame ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer. frame none (default) keeps the picture as it is; rounded cuts the screen's corners round with the radius of the model the phone runs as (square for the Home-button phone) and makes outside them transparent; device also puts a plain black bezel around it, a drawing with rounded outer corners and no buttons, not a picture of the phone. operations.title: Record virtual iOS device screen
operations.description: Record the running virtual iPhone's screen for seconds into an H.264 MP4 at path, as a durable job: the frames ios.emulator.control frame with transport file gives a viewer, polled fps times a second and encoded by ffmpeg as they come (ffmpeg must be installed). A frame that has not changed, or a poll slower than one frame, repeats the last picture, so the video lasts as long as the recording; the guest itself draws about 10 changed frames a second on this host. The job's result names the file and counts frames_written, frames_captured and frames_distinct; a phone that stops ends the recording early with what it has (ended_early). Follow it with job.wait and job.logs. job.send stop ends the recording early and keeps the video recorded so far (stopped_early). One recording at a time. Refused with ios_virtual_not_running when the phone is off.
